purpose: Google Updater Service — polls Google servers in the background to auto-update Chrome and Google apps.
rationale: Setting to Manual stops boot-time update spikes while Chrome and Google apps still update normally when launched.

purpose: Google Updater Internal Service — companion background updater for Google desktop software.
rationale: Setting to Manual trims boot storm overhead without breaking Chrome self-updates.

purpose: Legacy Google Update Service — checks for updates to Google desktop applications.
rationale: Setting to Manual prevents boot-time update checks while preserving on-demand updates.

purpose: Microsoft Edge Update Service — checks for background updates to Edge and WebView2.
rationale: Setting to Manual avoids boot-time updater contention while Edge still updates when opened.

purpose: Adobe Acrobat Update Service — checks for and installs background updates to Adobe Acrobat and Reader.
rationale: Does not need to start automatically on every Windows boot; works on demand.

purpose: Adobe Genuine / Creative Cloud Update Service — background updater for Adobe Creative Cloud suites.
rationale: Switching to Manual stops 24/7 idle background polling when Creative Cloud apps are closed.

purpose: Mozilla Maintenance Service — applies Firefox browser updates without UAC prompts.
rationale: Should remain Manual so it runs strictly when Firefox applies an update.

purpose: Logitech G HUB Updater Service — background self-updater daemon for Logitech G HUB.
rationale: When set to Automatic, holds ~45–60 MB RAM 24/7; Manual allows G HUB to update on demand when opened.

purpose: Logi Options+ Updater Service — background updater for Logitech Options+ mouse/keyboard software.
rationale: Switching from Automatic to Manual reduces login startup contention.

purpose: Muse Hub Authorization Service — background DRM/licensing daemon for MuseScore and Audacity plugins.
rationale: Burns noticeable CPU and RAM on every boot when Automatic; Manual starts it only when Muse Hub is used.

purpose: Muse Hub Updater Service — background self-updater for the Muse Hub client.
rationale: Only needed on demand when updating Muse Hub.

purpose: Camo Helper Service — virtual camera helper for using a smartphone as a PC webcam.
rationale: Only needed when Camo Studio is actively running; Manual avoids boot startup overhead.

purpose: Windows Subsystem for Linux Service — manages WSL2 Linux virtual machines (vmmemWSL).
rationale: When Automatic, can boot WSL2 at startup holding 1–4+ GB RAM; Manual frees boot RAM while still starting WSL seamlessly whenever 'wsl' is invoked.

purpose: NVIDIA LocalSystem Container — hosts NVIDIA App / GeForce Experience background tasks and ShadowPlay overlay.
rationale: Switching to Manual trims background CPU/RAM spikes if always-on ShadowPlay instant replay is not needed, while core GPU driver (NVDisplay.ContainerLocalSystem) remains Automatic.

purpose: Apple Mobile Device Service — background USB sync daemon for iTunes and iOS devices.
rationale: Notorious for running 24/7 as Automatic; Manual saves continuous idle CPU/RAM unless actively syncing an iPhone over USB.

purpose: Apple Bonjour mDNSResponder — local network zero-config service discovery for Apple AirPrint/iTunes.
rationale: Switching to Manual prevents 24/7 UDP multicast background listening when Apple sync apps are closed.

purpose: Steam Client Service — installs game redistributables and anti-cheat components for Steam games.
rationale: Should remain Manual so it runs strictly when Steam launches a game.

purpose: Epic Games Updater — background self-updater for the Epic Games Launcher.
rationale: Should remain Manual so it only runs when Epic Games Launcher is opened.

purpose: Epic Online Services — cross-play overlay and matchmaking helper for Epic titles.
rationale: Should remain Manual so it runs strictly on demand during gameplay.

purpose: EA Background Service — game library sync and background downloader for the EA App.
rationale: Switching to Manual stops background RAM/network usage when not playing EA titles.

purpose: Razer Game Manager Service — scans installed games and applies Razer Cortex/Synapse profiles.
rationale: Switching to Manual avoids continuous background polling when not using Razer Cortex.
